premises.text: Existing piezoelectric Braille interfaces are expensive ($5–8k) and show only a few words at a time, constraining literacy
premises.evidence_span: it's a $5,000 up to $8,000 keyboard. And where a blind person can read, it's extremely limited to just a few words

premises.text: A membrane bonded to an electrical actuator with airflow controls thousands of Braille dots without mechanical elements on a tactile tablet with touchscreen voiceover control
premises.evidence_span: We're using a high-performance membrane bonded to an electrical actuator so that through an airflow channel, we can control and deform each braille dot individually

premises.text: Cloud Braille converter turns text, documents, and web pages into full-page Braille on the device
premises.evidence_span: It can convert anything into Brow, like text files, documents, even whole web pages

premises.text: At about $500, GTM starts online then scales via global distributors and into developing-country education demand
premises.evidence_span: with the affordable price of $500 US

value.text: Blind users can learn, work, and play on one affordable device that outputs a whole Braille page
value.evidence_span: allows blind users for the first time to learn, work, and play with one single device

secondary_value.text: Open literacy and school access for blind children, including in developing countries
secondary_value.evidence_span: change the future of millions of children

causal_links.evidence_span: leads to low literacy rate among blind children
bring the tablet to the hands of millions

notes: Price and few-word limits folded as one piezoelectric-interface pain. Actuator membrane and thousands-of-dots tablet UI folded as one hardware mechanism; Braille converter kept as separately revisable software module. $500 + online/distributor/developing-country path kept as commercial package. Kenya 10k request treated as traction evidence not premise. Social-mission framing recorded in secondary_value.
